headline: High-risk default interaction: LangGraph can route ComfyUI outputs into writable, networked agent workflows, creating dangerous cascading errors and potential data leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/shared-channel surface, while LangGraph is a library that only ingests what the developer wires into its graph. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not default, but if ComfyUI outputs are manually copied into a LangGraph node or file-backed state, malicious text could be reinterpreted. The pathway is unusual and bounded.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into a LangGraph node or prompt field
IF LangGraph nodes parse ComfyUI output as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs as images/binaries, not prompt text
Add a delimiter/serialization step before any LangGraph ingestion
Disable any node that auto-prompts from upstream text
Review the graph for manual copy-paste bridges

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts locally, while LangGraph can read files and send data to model providers or developer-defined tools. If both share a workspace or checkpointer, sensitive media or checkpoints can flow from A into B and then out to third parties. This is plausible in default LangGraph deployments and the blast radius can include multiple work products.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in a directory that LangGraph reads
IF LangGraph nodes forward those artifacts or derived state to model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate ComfyUI and LangGraph storage directories
Restrict LangGraph nodes from reading media/checkpoints
Turn off any node that uploads file contents
Use a non-shared checkpointer namespace
Audit outbound tool calls for media payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI itself does not write the filesystem, but LangGraph can write files and spawn subprocesses, and its shared checkpointer enables concurrent instances. If the graph is wired to mutate the same application-defined files or state that ComfyUI workflows depend on, conflicts can occur. The overlap is not guaranteed, but the framework makes it easy to create mutable shared state without locking.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes write to the same directory or state store used by ComfyUI workflows
IF multiple LangGraph instances share the same checkpointer or application state
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories per agent
Use per-run checkpointer namespaces
Add file locks around shared state writes
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator
Keep ComfyUI assets read-only during graph execution

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where each node may itself be an agent, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative unless the developer adds verification. ComfyUI produces generated artifacts and workflow outputs that LangGraph may consume as inputs; if those outputs are used to drive actions or downstream agents, errors can cascade into irreversible or externally visible mistakes. The pair therefore has a dangerous default composition path.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes ComfyUI outputs without a verification step
IF downstream LangGraph nodes take actions based on generated artifacts or captions
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before action-taking nodes
Require schema validation on all ComfyUI outputs
Mark generated content as untrusted metadata
Separate generation and execution graphs
Log provenance for every upstream artifact

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is open-source and can run fully offline, but LangGraph commonly sends prompts or state to model providers and handles API keys. If regulated media or personal data from ComfyUI enters LangGraph, residency and retention obligations can diverge across provider backends. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their interaction, not either one alone.
conditions: IF regulated data from ComfyUI is passed into LangGraph
IF LangGraph routes that data to a provider with different residency or retention terms
mitigations: Block regulated data from entering LangGraph
Use a provider with matching residency terms
Set short retention on model-provider logs
Document the data flow for each graph edge
Add a preflight compliance checklist
